subject: English
passage: In response to concerns that students in many districts were struggling with standardized test performance, education policymakers have implemented mandatory tutoring programs designed to provide additional academic support. Zainab Musa et al. investigated the effectiveness of these tutoring interventions across multiple school districts and found that the programs produced only modest and temporary improvements in student achievement. Musa et al. argued that such programs may still be worthwhile to continue, given the minimal administrative burden of maintaining them.
prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It identifies a specific tutoring approach that Musa et al. may not have thoroughly examined in their research.
choices.B: It describes a consideration that explains why Musa et al. endorsed tutoring programs even though their benefits may be small relative to their administrative costs.
choices.C: It points out a factor that Musa et al. suggested may make tutoring programs more successful than their study indicates.
choices.D: It notes a factor that led Musa et al. to not dismiss tutoring programs altogether despite their evidence of the programs' limited effectiveness.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it most accurately describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole. The text establishes that many districts have implemented mandatory tutoring programs due to concerns about student test performance. According to the text, Musa et al. found that the effects of such programs on student achievement were modest and temporary. The text then adds that the researchers argue that because the administrative burden of maintaining the programs is minimal, the approach may be worth continuing even if the effects are limited. Thus, the underlined portion notes a factor—very low administrative burden—that led the researchers to not completely dismiss tutoring programs despite their evidence of limited effectiveness.
